name: MelaNone
tagline: A limb-scanning chamber that builds a 3D model of arm or leg skin and flags spots that may be melanoma.
problem: Melanoma is caught late; the team asked why airport-scanner-style imaging is not used for skin.
solution: Cameras capture a limb from many angles, stitch a 3D model, and a trained model classifies detected spots as likely benign or concerning, with a summary interface.
demo_moment: Team-described: place an arm in the chamber and see flagged spots on the 3D model.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Won “[Telus] The Edge of Innovation” among 169 submissions.
Borrowed the idea from an airport body scanner.

lessons: Medical demos need clear limits: screening support, not diagnosis.
